newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Avgold to close Loraine early due weak gold.
newsitem.headline: Avgold to close Loraine early due weak gold.

text.p: Avgold Ltd said on Tuesday the current weak gold price would force it to close parts of its Loraine division within 11-23 months, cutting short the mine's estimated three-year remaining life.
The company emphasised that closure related only to those areas of Loraine not incorporated in the neighbouring northern Free State Target gold project, due to start production in mid-1999.
"Current low gold prices have caused a revision...and a decision has been made to implement closure over an 11-23 month period," said Tim Spindler, manager of Avgold's mine operations.
Bullion ended trading in London on Tuesday at $326.45 an ounce, having touched a 12 year low of around $314 earlier this month.
"This 11-23 months life could be shortened considerably if there is no turnaround by the end of the current quarter."
Loraine has fallen into a 6.72 million rand ($1.5 million) loss in the year to date as at June 30, 1997.
Shareholders were informed in Avgold's Listing Particulars dated October 15, 1996 that Loraine had an estimated three-year life of mine at a gold price of 52,245 rand per kg.
Avgold said total gold production in 1998 would be 967,000 ounces of gold, in 1999 it would be 949,000 ounces but would fall in 2000 to 784,000 ounces when areas of Loraine are closed.

"We are considering various options besides Target and Sun (northern Free State gold projects) to reverse this decline. Any production acquired would have to have substantially lower costs," said David Kovarsky, investment relations manager.
In 2001 total Avgold output is seen at 833,000 ounces and in 2002 output is expected to be 875,000 ounces.

Over the next six months Avgold's output is expected to increase with the company's Hartebeestfontein division offsetting production declines at the Loraine and Eastern Transvaal Consolidated (ETC) divisions.

Avgold said that it planned to raise production in 1997 by an additional 4.8 tonnes as part of the recent productivity-linked wage deal signed earlier this month between the Chamber of Mines and the National Union of Mineworkers.
The deal calls for an additional 90 tonnes of gold output industry-wide for 1997 in return for wage increases of between nine and 25 percent.
Avgold said 3.6 tonnes of its additional output would come from Hartebeestfontein and 1.2 tonnes would come from Loraine.
Exploration results at Target and Sun were positive.

"Indications are that both Target and Sun can deliver at a cash cost of well below $200 an ounce. This could put them among the lowest cost producers in South Africa and place them in the lower cost quartile of gold producers internationally," Avgold said.

For the June quarter, Avgold made a net loss of 1.1 million rand compared to a net profit of one million rand in the preceding quarter. Capital spending in the quarter grew to 62.63 million rand from 34.42 million in the previous quarter.
Gold output was 7,237 kg compared to 7,234 kg, while costs rose to 51,652 rand/kg from 50,819 rand/kg.
"On paper it was a disappointing quarter. Gold production was static and costs rose slightly," Spindler said.
Avgold emphasised that its mines' infrastructure and ore reserves could be more fully utilised and that this may include operating throughout the calendar year for as many hours a day as possible.
"We hope to be able to introduce something shortly," said Avgold director Jurie Geldenhuys.
-- Johannesburg newsroom +27 11 482-1003 ($ = 4.580 South African Rand)
